svg.title: VesselSim builds vessel trees from a persistent random walk
svg.desc: Left: two synthetic 2-D vessel trees grown from the same random seed by recursive branching. Each segment is a random walk whose heading is rotated by a small random angle at every step, and line width is proportional to vessel radius. With a heading noise of 4 degrees per step the vessels are nearly straight; with 9 degrees they become tortuous, while the branching pattern and radii stay the same. Right: a single branch point in which a parent of radius 1.00 splits into daughters of radius 0.85 and 0.73, chosen so that the cubes of the daughter radii sum to the cube of the parent radius, as Murray's law requires.
svg.text: same seed, same branching and radii; only the heading noise differs
Murray's law at every branch point
VesselSim learns vessel shape from a persistent random walk with Murray-scaled radii
Each step turns the heading: d(s+1) = R(a, θ) d(s), a small random angle θ about a random axis a; branching odds fall with depth
Trees are rendered with random backgrounds, noise and skull shells, so shape is fixed while intensity varies. At test time only the
instance-norm γ, β are tuned on a masked-cube reconstruction loss: the shift is assumed to live in feature mean and scale, not in shape.
